description:
## Context

Two small structural issues identified in `Interactive`:

### 1. `maybe_suspend/1` is a no-op stub called on every frame

`advance/1` (`interactive.ex` L638) calls `maybe_suspend(state)` before every render. The implementation (`L880`) is:

```elixir
defp maybe_suspend(state), do: state
```

It does nothing. It runs on every `handle_info`/`handle_call` cycle.

### 2. `handle_call({:ui_request})` calls `render_frame` in two branches

`interactive.ex` L555–567:

```elixir
case reply do
  :pending ->
    new_state = put_dialog_from(new_state, from)
    new_state = render_frame(new_state)          # branch A
    {:noreply, new_state, loader_timeout(new_state)}

  val ->
    new_state = render_frame(new_state)          # branch B
    {:reply, val, new_state, loader_timeout(new_state)}
end
```

Both branches call `render_frame` after state mutation. They differ only in whether `put_dialog_from` runs first and whether the reply is `:noreply` or `{:reply, val}`. The structure obscures that render always happens.

## Implementation

### For `maybe_suspend/1`

Remove the call from `advance/1` and delete the `maybe_suspend/1` definition. If suspend is implemented in future it can be re-added at that time with a real body.

### For `handle_call({:ui_request})`

Refactor to make the render unconditional and vary only the response:

```elixir
{new_state, reply} = handle_ui_request(state, msg)

new_state =
  case reply do
    :pending -> put_dialog_from(new_state, from)
    _ -> new_state
  end

new_state = render_frame(new_state)

case reply do
  :pending -> {:noreply, new_state, loader_timeout(new_state)}
  val -> {:reply, val, new_state, loader_timeout(new_state)}
end
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `maybe_suspend/1` definition and its call site in `advance/1` are both deleted
- `handle_call({:ui_request})` contains exactly one `render_frame` call
- All existing Interactive tests pass
- No behaviour change observable from outside `Interactive`
title: Structural cleanup: remove maybe_suspend/1 stub; unify render_frame call in handle_call ui_request
